A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same controllable speech synthesis survey. Their complete text, figures, tables, and references support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Figure 1 presents the survey's own descriptive aggregation of methods by year and control attribute. This constitutes original literature data analysis, although the paper does not report original TTS benchmark experiments.

after.justification: Figure 1 retains updated method statistics and adds annual counts of DBLP entries matching a specified keyword. These are original descriptive analyses; synthesis performance findings elsewhere are attributed to cited work.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a synthesis algorithm or model. Expanded descriptions and revised classifications of surveyed architectures do not establish changes to a method developed by this work.

E1.justification: For the survey's descriptive data analysis, Figure 1 extends method coverage from 2018–2024 through March 2025 and adds a separate population of DBLP publication records. Additional speech corpora in v2 Table VI are surveyed resources, not newly used training or test datasets.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Additions and removals in the architecture catalogues change literature coverage, rather than membership in an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: The new bibliometric analysis specifies annual counting of DBLP entries matching 'controllable text-to-speech' over 2019–March 2025. This adds a sampling and aggregation protocol. Expanded descriptions of TTS metrics in Section V.B do not represent metrics newly applied in synthesis experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a supplementary analysis of publication volume over time, beyond v1's summary of control attributes across years. Neither version supplies original model ablations or robustness tests; v2's future-challenges diagram is conceptual synthesis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its analyses. The added explanations of means and covariance in evaluation metrics are not applied uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds DBLP counts, including 2 entries in 2019, 12 in 2024, and 3 through March 2025, plus control-attribute statistics for 2025. Section IV also newly summarizes cited findings about TP-GST listener preference and VoiceCraft edit naturalness. These are added descriptive and literature results, not same-setting TTS performance improvements.

T1.justification: Sections IV.A–B add explicit probabilistic formulations of NAR and AR sequence generation, including the AR conditional factorization in Equation 2; v1 provides verbal descriptions. This is a limited formal addition without new proofs or theorems. The standard metric formulas added in Section V.B are explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claim of a first comprehensive controllability-focused TTS survey covering architectures, control strategies, datasets, metrics, challenges, and future directions. Expanded supporting material does not redefine that central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 broadens style tagging from categorical labels to continuous and latent controls, distinguishes quantization from tokenization, and adds streaming limitations and adversarial attack/defense implications. It drops the separate environment-dataset category and removes v1 Section VII.B's acknowledgments of missing unified benchmarking and insufficient attribute/disentanglement analysis. Most existing challenge interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Table II adds code-access links for Whisper Encoder, Data2vec, Mimi Codec, and WavTokenizer. Tables III–IV provide more specific or revised architecture, vocoder, and feature-representation information. These improve documentation of surveyed resources without introducing an original implementation or training configuration.

R1.justification: The literature synthesis expands substantially across recent systems, tokenizers, speech editing, speech LLMs, datasets, metrics, and security research. Examples include DrawSpeech, DiffStyleTTS, Spark-TTS, Step-Audio, InstructSpeech, and FunAudioLLM. Earlier entries are also revised or omitted, including Bailing-TTS. The survey's positioning relative to earlier TTS surveys remains broadly unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 contains widespread language editing and substantial expansion or rewriting of control-strategy, dataset, evaluation, and application explanations. Section IV separates NAR, AR, and control strategies into subsections and moves the HMM discussion; Section VII becomes Applications and Security Issues, with the survey-limitations subsection removed. Author and contribution information also changes.

P2.justification: V2 adds the LLM architecture diagram in Figure 3, the future-direction/challenge diagram in Figure 6, and the control-signal summary in Table V. Figure 1 gains a publication-count plot and extends its statistics. Architecture, dataset, and metric tables are expanded or reformatted; v1's control taxonomy and challenges diagrams are retained as revised Figures 4 and 5.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the central survey more useful by explaining continuous and latent controls missing from v1's narrow style-tagging account and connecting methods to clearer component and control-signal summaries. These gains are tempered by removal of explicit survey limitations and new metric errors: Table VII marks cosine similarity as lower-is-better despite the opposite statement in Section V.B, and the PESQ range changes from typically 1–4.5 to [-0.5, -4.5]. The explanatory gains support a modest overall improvement, with uneven technical reliability.
